A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProtoFair and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references supporting a reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original ProtoFair experiments on CelebA and UTKFace in Tables 1–3 and representation visualizations in Figure 2, alongside baselines attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original results for BarlowTwins/BYOL, NIH Chest X-rays, sensitive-attribute prediction, and hyperparameter sensitivity.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same prototype initialization and EMA updates, cross-group positive-pair construction, detached assignments, within-batch and queue losses, and warmup procedure. Applying the regularizer to additional SSL objectives does not introduce a documented algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: v2 adds NIH Chest X-rays for pneumothorax prediction with patient sex as the sensitive attribute, substantially extending evaluation beyond facial images into medical imaging. Existing CelebA attribute tasks and UTKFace imbalance scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: New Table 3 evaluates standalone BarlowTwins and BYOL against their ProtoFair variants, extending comparisons to two noncontrastive SSL objectives. BYOL appeared only as future work in v1. Comparator membership in the original CelebA and UTKFace comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include controlled sweeps over K={3,5,10,15} and lambda={0,0.1,0.3,0.7,1}, frozen-feature sensitive-attribute linear probing, and medical evaluation using AUROC and sex-group AUROC gap. The original CelebA and UTKFace splits, metrics, and reported training schedules are retained.

E4.justification: v1 deferred systematic hyperparameter ablations to future work. v2 adds Section 4.5 and Figure 3 testing cluster-count and fairness-weight sensitivity across four CelebA attribute pairs, plus Table 6 quantitatively testing sensitive-attribute predictability. Existing t-SNE and UTKFace imbalance analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability estimates. The added tables and ablation curves retain point-estimate reporting without uncertainty bars.

E6.justification: All original table values are retained; UTKFace Table 3 becomes Table 4. New Table 3 reports lower EO for all eight BarlowTwins/BYOL task combinations. Table 5 reports SupCon versus SupCon+ProtoFair AUROC of 0.70 versus 0.72 and EO of 1.87 versus 1.79. Table 6 adds reduced sensitive-probe accuracy, and Figure 3 adds sensitivity curves showing accuracy losses at large fairness weights.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9), the positive-set definitions, prototype updates, loss formulations, and cluster-content assumption are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, derivation, or formal fairness guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction's empirical contribution now explicitly includes medical imaging, and the conclusion extends demonstrated compatibility to BarlowTwins and BYOL. The abstract and central claims about a target-label-free plug-in regularizer and clustering-based pseudo-counterfactual pairs remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets sensitive-probe reductions as reduced retained sensitive information and large fairness weights as overconstraining representations. The cluster-quality limitation remains, but v1's explicit qualification about setting-dependent warmup and training-schedule tuning is replaced by a shorter warmup-mitigation statement.

D1.justification: v2 supplies settings for the new BarlowTwins/BYOL experiments: 10 clusters, 100 warmup epochs, 5–15 additional fairness-training epochs, and method-specific weights of 0.2 or 0.3. It also describes the frozen-feature sensitive probe. Shared implementation details are unchanged; no ProtoFair code-access or hardware information is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Barlow Twins and the NIH chest X-ray dataset and removes the Jigsaw and generative-pretraining references associated with v1's future-work paragraph. BYOL changes from a proposed future evaluation to an evaluated method. Positioning relative to PCL, FSCL, adversarial debiasing, and counterfactual fairness remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 tightens wording throughout, condenses the qualitative discussion, adds an ablation subsection, and rewrites future work around autonomous driving and human-robot interaction. The main section order and most methodological and related-work prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Three new result tables (3, 5, and 6) and a four-panel ablation figure substantially expand the visual presentation. Existing tables and surrounding text are repositioned, UTKFace is renumbered Table 4, and captions are shortened. The architecture diagram and t-SNE plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 claimed broad plug-in applicability but tested only contrastive base objectives and explicitly deferred sensitivity studies. v2's BarlowTwins/BYOL comparisons and hyperparameter sweeps address these important evidence gaps, while sensitive-attribute probes strengthen the representation analysis beyond t-SNE. The medical experiment adds domain breadth. Sparse medical/probe implementation details, absent uncertainty estimates, and a less specific tuning caveat limit confidence, but the new evidence substantially strengthens support for the central claims.
